A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StructLoRA study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable despite formatting changes and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same IB-guided gates, graph construction, residual message passing, training objectives, and merging procedure for inference. Capitalizing the method name does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: The language, vision, and multimodal datasets remain unchanged, as do the low-data, varying-rank, long-context, and MT-Bench scenarios. Newly added benchmark citations do not introduce additional coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, filtering comparisons, coordination alternatives, and compatibility experiments. Newly cited methods such as AuroRA and UoRA are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A and I retain the same models, adaptation targets, ranks, data fractions, context lengths, splits, metrics, optimization settings, and parameter-budget controls.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component, GNN-design, filtering, and coordination ablations, plus the same long-context, singular-value, attention, gradient-similarity, and instruction-response analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 2's caption drops the statement that error bars indicate 95% confidence intervals. The identical plot contains no visible error bars, so this corrects its description. Three-seed averaging and the paired two-sided tests described in Appendix A remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–13 match. The six embedded figure images are identical, and Figure 7 retains the same responses and GPT-4 scores. No reported results or rankings change.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, drift-energy definitions, variational derivations, Theorem 1 and its proof, and oversmoothing and complexity arguments are retained. Equation reformatting does not alter their substance.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same dual-component contribution, mitigation of semantic drift and structural incoherence, superior PEFT performance especially at low ranks and limited data, and zero additional inference cost.

C2.justification: The explanations of filtering and coordination, interpretations of robustness and generalization, and claimed applicability remain unchanged. Both retain the same limitation concerning training overhead at larger scales.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link on the title page. Implementation details, hyperparameters, software, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an additional code or data release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited literature with benchmark sources, additional representation-learning citations, and numerous PEFT, reasoning, retrieval, multimodal, and generative-model references, principally in Appendix L. This broadens the bibliography while retaining the existing research-positioning narrative.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract and introduction, revises the title and author information, standardizes the method-name styling, and adds acknowledgments. The existing Impact Statement moves from Appendix M to the main text; most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing tables receive grouped headings, metric-direction arrows, and formatting refinements. Appendix table captions move above their tables, Figure 2 is enlarged and relocated, and Figure 6 moves. The underlying illustrations, plots, and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves presentation and documentation through clearer table headings, copyediting, and a project-page link. It also corrects Figure 2's misleading confidence-interval description, matching the unchanged plot without error bars. The expanded bibliography leaves the central positioning intact, while experiments, results, and theory remain unchanged; the overall gains are therefore limited.
